2yr.name: 2-year design storm
2yr.short: Synthetic 24 h rain, 3.5 in, 50% chance in any year
2yr.long: A made-up, smooth 24-hour rain, not a real day. Total 3.5 in (89 mm), peak 0.29 in/hr (7.4 mm/hr). Depth: NOAA Atlas 14 for Warren County, KY. Its return period is 2 years: rain this heavy has about a 50% chance of happening in any given year. That is an average, not a schedule: a 2-year storm can happen two years in a row. The return period describes the rainfall only, not how bad the flood is.
2yr.honesty: A design storm is a statistical yardstick, not a forecast or a real day. Not validated for depth. One comparison to the April 2025 flood (21 reported flooded roads) shows the model puts more water on flooded roads than on typical roads (AUC 0.84), which is a weak sign it finds where water collects, not proof of accurate depths.

context.text: No flood reports were found in a quick search for this day. Nothing here says it flooded.

validation.title: How well does the model match the real flood?
lines: 16 of 21 reported flooded roads reach 30 cm in the model, versus 27 of 100 random roads.
At 10 cm, all 21 reported roads are flagged, but so are 42 of 100 random roads, so 10 cm does not tell them apart.
Median road maximum depth: 0.62 m on reported flooded roads vs 0.08 m on random roads.
limits: The model replays 4.97 in of rain in 24 h; the real event brought about 10.5 in over four days at the airport.
There is no river inflow, so Barren River flooding is not captured.
The observations say a road was closed or flooded, not how deep the water was.
